# Ultimate-frisbee career on shelf, UFC on FOX 3's Pascal Krauss returns a motivated man

Steven Marrocco

USA TODAY Sports

[Share to Twitter](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmmajunkie.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fufc%2F2012%2F04%2F30%2Fultimate-frisbee-career-on-shelf-ufc-on-fox-3s-pascal-krauss-returns-a-motivated-man%2F82495259007%2F&text=Ultimate-frisbee%20career%20on%20shelf%2C%20UFC%20on%20FOX%203%27s%20Pascal%20Krauss%20returns%20a%20motivated%20man&via=MMAJunkie)[Share by email](mailto:?subject=Ultimate-frisbee%20career%20on%20shelf%2C%20UFC%20on%20FOX%203's%20Pascal%20Krauss%20returns%20a%20motivated%20man%20-%20from%20MMA%20Junkie&body=Ultimate-frisbee%20career%20on%20shelf%2C%20UFC%20on%20FOX%203's%20Pascal%20Krauss%20returns%20a%20motivated%20man%0A%0APascal%20Krauss%20made%20one%20appearance%20in%20the%20UFC%20%E2%80%93%20in%20November%202010.%20That's%20when%20he%20outpointed%20British%20welterweight%20Mark%20Scanlon%20at%20UFC%20122.%20But%20it%20might%20as%20well%20have%20been%20a%20decade%20ago%2C%20and%20back%20then%2C%20Facebook%20wasn't%20ev%0A%0ACheck%20out%20this%20story%20on%20mmajunkie.usatoday.com%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fmmajunkie.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fufc%2F2012%2F04%2F30%2Fultimate-frisbee-career-on-shelf-ufc-on-fox-3s-pascal-krauss-returns-a-motivated-man%2F82495259007%2F)

![](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/images/smg/2025/03/17/SMMA/82495254007-91-56200.jpeg?width=300&height=453&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

Pascal Krauss made one appearance in the UFC – in November 2010.

That's when he outpointed British welterweight Mark Scanlon at UFC 122. But it might as well have been a decade ago, and back then, Facebook wasn't even streaming preliminary-card fights.

So for all but the most hardcore of hardcores, the 25-year-old Krauss (10-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC) is making his octagon debut at UFC on FOX 3, which takes place Saturday at IZOD Center in East Rutherford, N.J.

Luckily, FUEL TV is broadcasting this fight (prior to the FOX-televised main card), and a sizably bigger audience will get to watch the undefeated German "Panzer" do his thing.

Standing opposite him is 24-year-old John Hathaway (15-1 MMA, 5-1 UFC), a once red-hot prospect who hasn't fought since March 2011. Like Krauss, his return has been blocked by injury.

Now less than a week from a bout against a fighter who's beaten the likes of established vets such as Rick Story and Diego Sanchez, Krauss is contemplating ring rust. It's a reasonable concern for anyone getting back into the cage after a six-month layoff, let alone the amount of time he's been off. He could be halfway to an undergraduate degree by now.

Or a couple more years away from finishing it, as is the case with him in Germany. Just a few months ago, he found Roufusport Academy in Milwaukee, where he's spent the bulk of his training camp.

"I've got a lot of good sparring right now, and I hope that helps," Krauss told [MMAjunkie.com Radio](http://www.mmajunkie.com/radio) (www.mmajunkie.com/radio). "Maybe I'll need a few minutes to get into it again, but hopefully not."

It was more of a challenge to begin training the right way than rush back too soon. Late this past year, Krauss injured the acromioclavicular (AC) joint in his shoulder and was forced to spend six months on the bench after surgery, which scrapped a meeting with Hathaway at UFC 138. (Hathaway then injured himself and was forced to withdraw entirely from the event.)

"I tried to come back a little bit too early," he said. "You feel good for a couple of weeks, but then you overtrain it, and you have a setback. It was kind of like that. But now, I feel really good again."

Good enough to accompany new training partner and Bellator champ Ben Askren to the field for a few games of his beloved frisbee golf.

"I wasn't good at that game, I confess," Krauss said. "He whooped our asses."

No doubt Askren's smothering, grinding mat work provided a challenge in the gym, as well.

So Krauss has been pushed, but he hasn't gone truly "live" for a long time. But if there's any comfort to take, it's that his opponent hasn't exactly been active.

"That's a pretty good matchup for me because of that," he said. "\[Hathaway\] beat some tough guys. But I definitely think I can beat him, and it will be a big step up for me in competition. I look forward to showing what Germany is able to do in MMA."

The first time Krauss stepped into the octagon, he was denied a finish for the first time in his professional career. He did, however, get a bonus for "Fight of the Night."

Could Hathaway be his coming-out party, for real?

![](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/images/smg/2025/03/11/SMMA/82261430007-91-196332.jpeg?width=660&height=441&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

Veteran MMA referee Herb Dean will be the third man in the cage for UFC 216's main event between Tony Ferguson and Kevin Lee.

During a meeting today in Las Vegas, the Nevada State Athletic Commission tapped Dean to oversee the UFC interim lightweight title bout, which takes place Oct. 7 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. The main card airs live on pay-per-view following prelims on FS1 and UFC Fight Pass.

Dean, who's refereed dozens of high-profile UFC headliners, will receive $1,900 for his work.

[Video: UFC 215, UFC 216 media day face-offs, where Tony Ferguson and Kevin Lee get heated](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2017/08/video-ufc-215-ufc-216-tony-ferguson-kevin-lee-amanda-nunes-valentina-shevchenko-demetrious-johnson-ray-borg)

The NSAC also selected veteran judges Derek Cleary, Junichiro Kamijo and Chris Lee, who will receive $1,500 each, to score the fight.

Ferguson (23-3 MMA, 13-1 UFC) gets his second crack at UFC gold after an interim title fight with Khabib Nurmagomedov (24-0 MMA, 8-0 UFC) at UFC 209 [was ultimately canceled](http://mmajunkie.com/2017/03/khabib-nurmagomedov-hospitalized-after-weight-cut-ufc-209-title-fight-with-tony-ferguson-off) when Nurmagomedov fell ill and couldn't compete. The two jawed on Twitter about a potential fourth booking, but UFC President Dana White said [Nurmagomedov is "not ready,"](http://mmajunkie.com/2017/09/khabib-nurmagomedov-kevin-lee-tony-ferguson-interim-title-polite) opening the door for Lee (16-2 MMA, 9-2 UFC).

The first-time interim title challenger said there's a simpler explanation Nurmagomedov isn't fighting Ferguson.

"(Nurmagomedov's) just being a (expletive) about it," Lee [told MMAjunkie Radio](http://mmajunkie.com/2017/08/ufc-interim-title-challenger-kevin-lee-says-khabib-b-tched-out-and-doesnt-want-to-fight). "Bottom line, he doesn't want to fight. He wants to hold on to that imaginary zero that he's got."

The fight card for November's "UFC 122: Marquardt vs. Okami" event is now complete with 11 bouts.

The event takes place Nov. 13 at Konig Pilsener Arena in Oberhausen, Germany.

The night's main card, including a No. 1 contender's bout between middleweights Nate Marquardt and Yushin Okami that headlines the show, airs via same-day delay on Spike TV.

Co-headlining the event is another middleweight matchup with legit contenders: Jorge Rivera and Alessio Sakara. And rounding out the main card are lightweights Dennis Siver vs. Andre Winner, welterweights Amir Sadollah vs. Peter Sobotta and light heavyweights Krzysztof Soszynski vs. Goran Reljic.

The preliminary card includes light heavyweights Jason Brilz vs. Vladimir Matyushenko, welterweights Pascal Krauss vs. Kenny Robertson, welterweights Duane "Bang" Ludwig vs. Nick Osipczak, middleweights Rob Kimmons vs. Kyle Noke, light heavyweights Seth Petruzelli vs. Karlos Vemola, and welterweights Kris McCray vs. Carlos Eduardo Rocha.

Initially, UFC 122 was expected to feature a headliner between Okami and Vitor Belfort. But with top contender Chael Sonnen sidelined as he deals with the aftermath of a failed UFC 117 drug test, Belfort instead gets the next shot at champion Anderson Silva. As [MMAjunkie.com](http://mmajunkie.com/) (www.mmajunkie.com) [reported](http://mmajunkie.com/news/20838/frankie-edgar-defends-title-against-gray-maynard-at-ufc-125.mma) on Wednesday, that fight is expected to take place during Super Bowl weekend in February.

Marquardt took Belfort's spot because he suffered virtually no damage in a Sept. 15 UFC Fight Night 22 victory over Rousimar Palhares.

For more on each of the card's individual matchups, check out the [UFC 122](http://mmajunkie.com/event/744/ufc-122-in-oberhausen-germany.mma) section of the site for past story reports.

The full UFC 122 lineup includes:

MAIN CARD

- Nate Marquardt vs. Yushin Okami
- Jorge Rivera vs. Alessio Sakara
- Dennis Siver vs. Andre Winner
- Amir Sadollah vs. Peter Sobotta
- Krzysztof Soszynski vs. Goran Reljic

PRELIMINARY CARD (un-aired)

- Jason Brilz vs. Vladimir Matyushenko
- Pascal Krauss vs. Kenny Robertson
- Duane "Bang" Ludwig vs. Nick Osipczak

![](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/images/smg/2025/02/25/SMMA/80323280007-91-2806462.jpeg?width=1320&height=744&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

SEATTLE – In the wake of Ilia Topuria's UFC featherweight title vacation, promotion CEO Dana White explained the company's stance on double champions Saturday following [UFC Fight Night 252](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/events/ufc-fight-night-february-22-2025).

White said the promotion isn't against fighters trying to vie for multiple championships, but indicated he expects an elevated level of activity from those who choose to attempt that feat.

"Unless you think you can defend your title," White told reporters including MMA Junkie backstage at Climate Pledge Arena. "If there's a guy who thinks he can do it and wants to defend both belts and has accomplished all these great things, I would have no problem with it. But you're going to be busy.

"... Unless you've really wiped out a division, like Jon Jones, who was in light (heavy)weight forever and then moved up to heavyweight. Ilia, I get it. It makes sense. Like I said, who he's beat and how he beat them, and now he's tired of making weight and wants to move up to 155? Totally makes sense. But no, I'm definitely not (against it). Weili Zhang, they just asked me. She's accomplished just about everything you can accomplish in her weight division and I don't have a problem with it. The philosophy hasn't changed, it's just on a case-by-case basis."

There have been four double champions in UFC history who have held two belts simultaneously: Henry Cejudo, Daniel Cormier, Conor McGregor and Amanda Nunes.

Topuria, 28, according to White, offered up his featherweight title as to not hold up the division. His exact next move in terms of matchmaking is not currently known.

http://mmajunkie.com Kyle Noke (18-4-1 MMA, 2-0 UFC) will fight on his home soil as part of a bout with Chris Camozzi (14-3 MMA, 2-0 UFC) at UFC 127 in Australia.

Noke announced the bout via Facebook on Monday.

Although not officially announced by the organization, UFC 127 is expected to take place Feb. 27 at Acer Arena in Sydney, Australia.

The event airs live on pay-per-view, though it's not clear if Noke vs. Camozzi will be part of the broadcast.

Noke entered the UFC as a cast member on "The Ultimate Fighter 11," where he was one of the most experienced fighters on the middleweights-only cast. After an upset loss to Kris McCray in the quarterfinal round of the show, the Australian returned at the TUF 11 Finale and defeated Josh Bryant via TKO. Recently, he moved to 2-0 in the UFC with a submission win over Rob Kimmons at UFC 122.

Noke now puts a four-fight win streak on the line against Camozzi, who also appeared on "TUF 11" (albeit briefly). After winning his elimination-round fight, Camozzi was forced off the show with a broken jaw. However, he got a spot at the TUF 11 Finale and scored a decision win over James Hammortree. Then at UFC 121, he picked up his second UFC victory (and fourth win overall) with a split-decision win over Dong Yi Yang.

For more on [UFC 127](http://mmajunkie.com/event/762/ufc-127-in-sydney-australia.mma), stay tuned to the [UFC Rumors](http://mmajunkie.com/Rumors) section of MMAjunkie.com.

(Photo by JOEL SAGET / AFP) (Photo by JOEL SAGET/AFP via Getty Images)](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/gcdn/authoring/images/smg/2025/02/24/SMMA/80090964007-91-2656799.jpeg?width=1320&height=880&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp)

An internet offer recently became a reality, according to UFC Hall of Famer Georges St-Pierre.

Shown in an [Instagram post](https://www.instagram.com/p/CuQLly_vqrT/?igshid=MTIzZWMxMTBkOA%3D%3D) Monday, St-Pierre posed for a photo with billionaire and Tesla CEO Elon Musk after an apparent training session. Also pictured is esteemed jiu-jitsu instructor John Danaher and famed computer scientist-turned-podcaster Lex Fridman.

"Great training session with 3 men I really admire," St-Pierre wrote. "Combined IQ in this photo is 1000. Not including me."

Musk reacted to the photo's publication shortly therafter.

"Really fun!" Musk wrote on Twitter. "The obvious conclusion is that I need a \*lot\* more training."

St-Pierre [recently reached out to Musk](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2023/06/elon-musk-accepts-georges-st-pierres-offer-train-mark-zuckerberg-fight) to offer training services after the business magnate engaged in a mass attention-grabbing discourse about a potential fight against Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg.

"@elonmusk I’m a huge fan of yours and it would be an absolute honor to help you and be your training partner for the challenge against Zuckerberg," St-Pierre tweeted.

Shortly thereafter, Musk responded, "OK, let’s do it."

While there has been [no shortage of reactions](https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/lists/elon-musk-vs-mark-zuckerberg-fighters-react-ufc-jon-jones-dana-white-mma) from the MMA community since Musk and Zuckerberg first engaged in a sudden spark of cage fight-oriented discussions, there is not yet hard evidence an actual fight will take place.

UFC president Dana White has leaned into the idea and said he's since held discussions with both Musk and Zuckerberg about a potential fight. White and the UFC are now even selling "Musk vs. Zuckerberg" merchandise in their online store.
